authors.institution: Anhui University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: A Burns-Krantz theorem on convex domains
papers.abstract:
We prove two boundary rigidity theorems for holomorphic self-maps of bounded convex domains. Let $\Omega\subset\C^n$, $n\geq1$, and suppose that $\partial\Omega$ is $C^{1,\alpha}$ near $p\in\partial\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\leq1$. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ satisfies $f(z)=z+o(|z-p|^3)$ as $z\to p$ in one fixed non-tangential approach region at $p$, then $f=\id_\Omega$.
  We also prove a rigidity theorem for bounded convex domains $\Omega$ without assuming boundary smoothness. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ of $\Omega$ satisfies $f(z)-z=O(|z-p|^m)$ as $z\to p\in\partial\Omega$ for some $m>1+2\pi/\theta_p$, where $\theta_p$ is the supremum of sector angles in the open tangent cone at $p$, taken over complex lines through its vertex, then $f=\id_\Omega$, which proves a conjecture of Zimmer.

authors.name: Jianyong Qiao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: PANO: Parallel Latent Space Neural Operator for Solving PDEs
papers.abstract: Aggregating observations into a limited number of latent tokens and learning physical interactions in the latent space has emerged as an effective approach for Transformer-based neural operators to solve Partial Differential Equation (PDE) problems involving large-scale observations. However, existing methods typically compress observations using a single aggregation pattern, making physical information not retained by that pattern invisible to the latent space and thereby constraining physical interactions within it. To address this limitation, we propose PArallel Latent Space Neural Operator (PANO), a novel neural operator for solving PDEs that formulates physical interactions among observations as an additive combination of interaction results from parallel latent spaces with shared parameters. Specifically, PANO transforms observations into multiple distinct compressed representations through independent mappings, learns physical interactions in parallel based on these representations, and finally fuses the decoded results to predict the target physical field. Within PANO, we further propose Coupled Assignment Projection (CAP) to construct bidirectionally consistent encoding and decoding mappings, and Pairwise Latent Space Attention Layer (PaLA) to jointly update latent representations of each latent space through adaptive cross-space interactions. Extensive experiments on nine benchmarks spanning diverse physical systems, geometries, and observation scales demonstrate that PANO achieves state-of-the-art performance. Notably, PANO reduces equivalent plastic strain prediction errors on Unilateral Stamping by 28.3% (or more) and lift-coefficient prediction errors on AirCraft by 21.4% (or more) compared with existing methods. Code is available at https://github.com/ZijiangY1116/PANO.

authors.name: Zijiang Yang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Dongmei Fu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Long-Term Quantile Treatment Effects with Combined Experimental and Observational Data
papers.abstract: This paper studies the identification, estimation, and inference of long-term quantile treatment effects (LTQTEs) when short-term experimental data are supplemented with long-term observational data. Under a latent unconfoundedness framework, we establish identification of the LTQTE curve and derive the corresponding efficient influence functions. Building on these influence functions, we propose a semiparametrically efficient estimation procedure and develop a multiplier bootstrap method for uniform inference on the LTQTE curve, yielding valid simultaneous confidence bands over a continuum of quantile indices.

authors.name: Yanbo Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system with general bulk viscosity and Navier slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with Navier slip boundary conditions is established in a smooth bounded domain that may be multiply connected. Arbitrarily large initial data and vacuum are allowed, and the positive doping profile may have large spatial variations. The bulk viscosity satisfies a logarithmic derivative bound and a growth condition on its primitive, including every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with a logarithmic gain larger than one half. Time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponential convergence to the nonconstant hydrostatic state are obtained. For strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential convergence to the hydrostatic state in higher Sobolev norms are proved. An initial vacuum point persists and causes exponential growth of density gradients.

papers.title: Any2Building: Unifying Point Clouds and Images for Building Reconstruction via Shared Spatial Queries
papers.abstract: Abstracting structured buildings from limited observations is essential for 3D urban modeling and digital twins. Partial point clouds and overhead images of the same building provide incomplete 3D surface measurements and visual cues to its footprint, roof geometry, and rooftop structures, respectively. This motivates a unified framework that aligns geometric and visual cues in 3D and reconstructs buildings from either or both modalities. Building on this connection, we present Any2Building, a unified model for Level of Detail 2 (LoD2) building reconstruction from partial point clouds, overhead images, or both, with optional coarse geometric priors. At its core is an occupancy-grounded shared spatial queries representation that organizes available observations within a common 3D grid. Supervised by complete building surface voxels, these queries connect observational evidence to target geometry, enabling a shared generator to learn structural priors across tasks and providing spatial guidance for recovering missing structure. A trained voxel conditional surface-generation and low-poly remeshing pipeline then converts the predicted structure into compact LoD2 building models. To support this framework, we introduce BuildingWorld-Image, comprising approximately one million paired samples of partial point clouds, overhead images, and LoD2 building models across 18 cities. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that Any2Building outperforms existing methods in geometric reconstruction accuracy across unimodal and multimodal point-cloud completion, single-image building generation, and prior-assisted generation, while maintaining detailed and robust recovery when point cloud input modality is degraded.

authors.name: Tengxi Wang
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Permutation groups, derangements and connections
papers.abstract:
What is the chance that a random shuffling of a deck of cards leaves no card in its original place? More precisely, what is the chance that a random permutation has no fixed points? A permutation with no fixed points is known as a derangement. Questions about derangements, like the ones above, go back centuries, but there are also several unsolved problems in this very active area of permutation group theory.
  Based on a minicourse given at "Groups and Algebras in Bicocca for Young Algebraists" in June 2026, this survey provides a general introduction to permutation group theory, with a specific focus on derangements. The survey features modern methods for studying permutation groups, recent developments and open problems concerning derangements and connections between this topic and other areas, such as combinatorics, graph theory, number theory, representation theory and topology.

papers.title: Richtmyer-Meshkov instability induced by a Gaussian-kicked rotor-like potential in a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.abstract: This research investigates the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability within a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate. We offer a kicking potential that replicates the impulsive shock across both interfaces of the three-component BEC to trigger the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability. We propose a hydrodynamic model that indicates the essential criteria for the onset of hydrodynamic instability in the BEC through the application of the hydrodynamic pressure equation. We utilise the split-step Crank-Nicolson method to numerically solve the coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations, with the objective of obtaining the immiscible ground state of all components in a quasi-2D harmonic trap. Following this, we introduce a Gaussian-like disruption instigated by the kick rotor model at both interfaces of the confined three-component BEC to explore the time-dependent development of nonlinear hydrodynamic instability patterns, culminating in quantum turbulence and nonlinear configurations at the interfaces. The kinetic energy spectra of both the incompressible and compressible elements of the system exhibit scaling in the low-wavenumber domain with power-law exponents of $-5/3$ and $1$, respectively. Conversely, the high-wavenumber domain is defined by $k^{-4}$ and $k^{-7/2}$ scaling for the incompressible and compressible elements, respectively, aligning with the established spectral characteristics of quantum turbulence. This research offers fresh perspectives on the mechanisms of hydrodynamic instability, vortex generation, non-equilibrium pattern evolution, and quantum turbulence in superfluid systems comprising multiple interacting elements.

papers.title: BATMoS: Budget-Aware Guidance Allocation for Efficient Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of a video diffusion model's inference budget depends on where computation is spent along the denoising trajectory. Across eight equal-budget inference configurations, VBench total scores span 4.80 points, highlighting the importance of explicit allocation design. Our key insight is that guidance evaluations are not equally valuable across diffusion time: retaining the sampling updates while selectively reusing guidance can preserve generation quality with fewer denoiser evaluations. We introduce BATMoS (Budget Aware Temporal Mixture of Strategies), which routes between fresh classifier-free guidance and cached guidance using a single pretrained denoiser. A magnitude-based temporal rule assigns guidance reuse to low-magnitude blocks and reserves fresh guidance for the remaining blocks, with a single integer controlling the computation budget. The resulting schedule requires no additional router training or per-budget threshold search. Evaluated on CogVideoX-2B with 4,720 videos per configuration across all sixteen official VBench dimensions, BATMoS achieves the highest total score among the eight allocation policies and comes within 0.10 points of full classifier-free guidance using 20\% fewer branch evaluations. BATMoS also composes with feature reuse, reducing computation from 80 to 62 effective branch evaluations with a 0.11-point decrease in total score. These findings make temporal guidance allocation a practical mechanism for extracting more generation quality from a fixed inference budget.

authors.name: Jingwei Sun
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements
papers.abstract: Coordinating a team of heterogeneous agents to complete tasks with unknown requirements is a challenging multi-agent planning problem. Agents differ in their ability to discover task requirements and in their ability to engage tasks, so the planner must coordinate task discovery, execution, and staging. This paper introduces a hierarchical planner that uses a graph neural network policy to assign actions to agents, then finds a path to the action's location using a shortest-path algorithm. The central part of our approach is the CAAT graph, which is a graph representation of the planning context consisting of the agents, tasks, capabilities, and actions. We demonstrate that our learned planner can jointly coordinate a heterogeneous team to simultaneously discover task requirements and complete tasks in a shorter time compared to baselines that optimize task discovery and task engagement independently. Furthermore, we show that our policy can zero-shot plan on out-of-distribution settings by training only on an outdoor map then transferring without finetuning to an indoor map with more agents, tasks, and capabilities than seen during training.

papers.title: B-Series Theory for Continuous Time Integration Methods
papers.abstract: B-Series are a common tool for constructing numerical integration methods and partitioned variations. In this paper, we expand the operations of B-Series to describe the formal expansion of modified differential equations found in multirate ODE solvers. Typically, such modified differential equations have time dependent approximations using summed fixed constant states. To create the B-Series we introduce a new operation called replacement to induce the constant states and add a time parameterization to the labels of the B-Series. By doing so we introduce new analysis via the permanent and block matrices which provide alternative formulations to composition and substitution. To support the time dependent labels properties are provided, the exact solution is described in Tree Iterated Integrals, and the underlying approximate representations are analyzed.

papers.title: Edge-Combining Subharmonic Mixer-First Receiver
papers.abstract: A 1-10 GHz subharmonic mixer-first receiver using edge combining to drive N-path switches from 50% duty-cycle clocks at half the local oscillator (LO) frequency avoids the gain penalty of harmonic mixing. Inverter-based differential baseband amplifiers with back-gate feedback linearization set their gain by process-defined capacitance ratios, using no additional components and consuming no additional power. A 22 nm fully depleted silicon on insulator (FD-SOI) prototype receiver achieves a conversion gain of 12.8-18.1 dB and a noise figure of 5.7-11 dB across the band. It achieves up to 15.4 dBm out-of-band IIP3 while consuming 16.7-22.3 mW.

papers.title: Engineering third order absorbing exceptional points in multi-drive cavity magnonics for enhanced sensing
papers.abstract: We consider a four mode cavity magnonics system consisting of two coupled resonators containing a pair of YIG spheres. Each resonator has two input-output ports allowing for the application of multiple drive fields. We show that with control of the dipolar coupling strength between the YIG spheres the relative amplitude and phase of the drive fields can be used to tune the system to third order absorbing exceptional points. The system considered here offers considerable flexibility and may be useful for high sensitivity detection as absorbing exceptional points can avoid the eigenbasis collapse associated with their resonant counterparts.

papers.title: On Modelling the Far-Side Unsigned Magnetic Flux Evolution of Long-Lived NOAA Active Regions
papers.abstract: The evolution of magnetic flux in solar active regions is central to space-weather forecasting and solar-cycle studies. Direct measurements of the far-side magnetic field, however, remain unavailable with current solar instrumentation. We develop a method to estimate the far-side evolution of active-region magnetic flux using 304 {\AA} (He II) emission as a quantitative proxy. Using SDO/AIA and SDO/HMI observations of all four near-side passages of a long-lived active region (NOAA AR 12192), we fit a single relation that gives mean per-pixel unsigned magnetic flux from mean per-pixel 304 {\AA} intensity. The fit uses only disk-centre, flare-free intervals, and flux is the dependent variable, so the relation can be applied directly to intensity measurements. The magnetogram flux is deprojected to the radial direction before fitting, and we report the line-of-sight version for comparison. We first test the relation by fitting it on the first two passages and predicting the two later passages, which were not used in that fit; the relation adopted for the reconstruction is then fitted to all four passages. We then apply the same relation to STEREO-A/EUVI 304 {\AA} observations, scaling the EUVI intensities to AIA-equivalent boundary intensities inferred from the adjacent near-side flux measurements, and so reconstruct the unsigned flux history while the region was out of view from Earth. The test on the later passages gives a median log-space residual of +0.052 dex, a root-mean-square error of 0.083 dex, and a median absolute fractional error of 14% over 272 samples that were not used in the fit. Because a single cross-instrument scale factor cannot match both ends of a far-side interval, the absolute level of each reconstructed segment carries an uncertainty of several tens of per cent; it is the shape of the far-side curve, rather than its level, that the EUVI observations constrain.

papers.title: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
papers.abstract: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density profiles without directly evolving the dust as a fluid. We compare the GRTM with dust profiles computed via standard methods using the $\texttt{FARGO3D}$ code, which models the dust as a pressureless fluid, and find very good agreement over a wide range of parameter space. Finally, we investigate how dust gap formation depends on the planet-to-star mass ratio ($q$) and Stokes number ($\mathrm{St}$), through a parameter study, establishing an empirical criterion for dust gap opening. In doing so, we have discovered a new regime of gap opening for small grains with $St \lesssim 10^{-2}$ and for planet mass well below Jupiter's, which is likely very relevant for gaps seen in ALMA images.

papers.title: SIMQ: A Single Graph-based Index for Multi-Vector Query
papers.abstract: Multi-vector retrieval models such as ColBERT achieve state-of-the-art effectiveness by representing documents as sets of token-level vectors and scoring via MaxSim, but their high computational cost limits scalability to large corpora. Existing approximate methods face fundamental bottlenecks: centroid interaction matrix approaches require computing a full matrix at every query and rely on GPU-accelerated clustering, while data-oblivious compression methods yield unstable recall that requires repeated compensation. We propose SIMQ (Single graph Index for Multi-vector Query), a framework that bridges single-vector graph indices and multi-vector retrieval through data-aware sampling-based clustering and per-token graph navigation, simultaneously bypassing all aforementioned bottlenecks. SIMQ organizes all token vectors into fine-grained clusters via data-aware sampling, builds a single graph index over cluster centroids independently of PLAID's residual representation, and approximates the MaxSim score through per-token graph search without materializing any interaction matrix or relying on GPU acceleration. We provide theoretical analysis showing that, under a manifold assumption and successful cell retrieval, data-aware partitioning has a smaller expected approximation error than a data-oblivious partition. Building on this foundation, SIMQ+ further introduces count-based scoring and a dynamic candidate set to improve robustness across varying query conditions. Experiments on five benchmarks compare recall, throughput, and construction time against several baselines, primarily on CPU; large-scale PLAID k-means centroids are built on a separate GPU machine. SIMQ has been integrated into VSAG, an Ant Group's open-source vector search library.

authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Heng Tao Shen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: PCRG: Training-Free Pruning and Caching of Reference Tokens for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Reference-to-video diffusion transformers pack the variational autoencoder (VAE) latents of all references and the generated tokens into one full-attention sequence, in which reference tokens make up about half. Because attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length, these tokens take up an even larger share of the attention computation, yet most of them are static, smooth or irrelevant to the output. To accelerate reference-conditioned generation, we propose pruning and caching of reference tokens for video generation (PCRG), a training-free, plug-and-play method that uses two signals the model already computes to assign each reference token to one of three tiers, namely pruned, cached or kept. The first is a low-level redundancy r from VAE latents, since a token whose latent barely changes over time or across its neighbors adds little new content. The second is a high-level importance g from the vision-language-model (VLM) conditioner, where the attention that the prompt and any first or last frames pay to a token tells whether the output needs to read it. Tokens that are not redundant are kept, and redundant tokens are cached if important and pruned otherwise. Pruned tokens leave the sequence before the first step with all rotary position embedding positions unchanged. Cached tokens have their keys and values computed once and reused, and kept tokens are processed as usual. On MiniMax-H3, already distilled to 8 timesteps and quantized to int8, PCRG is 1.57x faster end to end on our V2V-Bench and 1.49x faster on the public VACE-Benchmark, while the quality of VBench drops by only 0.24% and 0.17%, respectively. PCRG shortens the sequence rather than changing how attention is computed or which steps are run, so it also stacks on step caching and sparse attention. On V2V-Bench it reaches 1.86x with TeaCache, 1.82x with Spark at nearly unchanged fidelity and 2.15x with Veda.

authors.name: Haoran Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: LaFlash: Capacity-Driven Acceleration for Coding Agent Workflows via QLC-HBF
papers.abstract:
As large language models (LLMs) evolve toward agentic AI, coding agents are emerging as memory-intensive workloads that repeatedly reuse persistent states, including contexts and KV caches. Emerging agentic workflows, including Loop/Graph Engineering, cause state amplification through frequent active/dormant transitions, increasing memory pressure. Evicted states incur costly recomputation upon reactivation, particularly under long-context, short-decode workloads. This motivates Capacity-Driven Acceleration (CDA), which explicitly accounts for state amplification to allocate memory capacity between active concurrency and dormant-state retention, replacing recomputation with memory access.
  In this work, we propose LaFlash, a High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) architecture that exploits the large capacity of Quad-Level Cell (QLC)-based flash to realize CDA. However, QLC's long read latency demands massive read parallelism under irregular state reactivation and varying context lengths, while limited write endurance constrains placement. LaFlash introduces Session Grouping to balance active request counts and aggregate context lengths across groups, sustaining read parallelism and block utilization through request-exclusive allocation. Furthermore, Fast-Page Allocation exploits QLC's read-latency heterogeneity to mitigate residual inter-group imbalance and sustain bandwidth utilization. On end-to-end coding agent workloads, LaFlash achieves 7.04$\times$ higher throughput and 10.96$\times$ higher energy efficiency over SLC-HBF with batch expansion, and 2.36$\times$ higher throughput over QLC-HBF with CDA. HBM buffering further reduces unnecessary NAND writes, improving QLC write endurance. These results demonstrate the benefits of jointly optimizing state retention and physical data placement for capacity-driven acceleration.

authors.name: Yuseon Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sanghyeon Park
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Seongyon Hong
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sangjin Kim
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
papers.abstract: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retaining impossibility judgments about unachieved capabilities. To test whether context management can elicit further capability, we propose SCoRe, which compacts context at stop bursts and marks these judgments as unproven. SCoRe improves verified capability over summary-based continuation and other evaluated context-management baselines. With SCoRe, MiMo reaches a capability coverage score of 67.0% at 2,000 turns, exceeding both 32.4% under the original stopping policy and the 58.6% computed for GPT-5.5 from ExploitBench's 300-turn reference results on the same tasks. These findings show that stopping need not mark an agent's exploitation limit, and that continued execution with context management can elicit substantial further capability.

authors.name: Deokhyung Kang
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Minjae Gwon
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sangdon Park
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling
papers.abstract: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed. The conditions under which the agents can combine their capabilities, however, are physical properties of the team and are known before any demonstration is collected. We encode the conditions as constraints on the team trajectories, and we enforce the constraints while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations of each agent alone. We prove that the proposed method can generate every team trajectory that satisfies the constraints, although the demonstrations contain no cooperation. Hence the constraints determine which team trajectories can be generated, and the demonstrations determine how likely each team trajectory is. Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show the effectiveness of the method, which generates cooperative team trajectories that satisfy the constraints and requires no retraining when agents join or leave the team. Finally, we implement the method on a multi-robot testbed.

authors.name: Magnus Egerstedt
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Solution Spaces of the Minimal Surface and Monge-Amp\`{e}re Equations near Infinity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the constructions of all solutions to the minimal surface equation and the Monge-Amp\`{e}re equation near infinity and the parametrization of these solutions by harmonic functions. It is well-known that Dirichlet boundary value problems in exterior domains do not always admit solutions. We demonstrate that prescribing asymptotic behaviors forms a new type of problem leading to all solutions near infinity. The harmonic functions determining the asymptotic behaviors play the role of ``free data" as the boundary values in the boundary value problems.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions II
papers.abstract: This is the second of two papers on isolated boundary singularities of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We construct positive solutions that violate the critical upper bound, proving that the dimension ranges in Part I are sharp. For general smooth metrics, the conformal metric can be incomplete near the singularity in every dimension $n\ge18$, and complete in every dimension $n\ge19$. For Euclidean domains with smooth boundary, both types exist for $n\ge23$. We also construct both types for metrics with totally geodesic boundary in dimensions $n\ge35$.

papers.title: Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering
papers.abstract: GRPO has become the dominant reinforcement learning method for eliciting reasoning capability in LLMs using verifiable rewards. However, it suffers from a fundamental failure mode: when a training question exceeds the base model's current capability, all generated responses fail and receive zero reward, yielding no gradient signal and stalling further capability expansion. An emerging class of GRPO extensions, termed Hint-Augmented GRPO (HA-GRPO), adds a "hint" to the context to reduce the difficulty of the question, thereby producing a usable gradient signal. Nevertheless, existing HA-GRPO methods share a key issue: no hint is available at inference time to append to the question, creating a training-inference context mismatch that leads to inconsistent performance gains. In this work, we reinterpret the function of hinting -- not as reducing question difficulty, but as steering model behavior -- and propose ASH (Activation Steering for Hinting), a novel HA-GRPO method built on this view. During training, the model is presented with both hinted and plain questions, while a trainable steering vector is optimized to widen the margins between the model's generation probabilities for responses to the hinted version relative to the plain version, thereby capturing the question-agnostic component of the behavioral shift induced by the hint. During inference, the trained steering vector is directly injected into the model's activation, reproducing the hint-conditioned behavior without requiring any hint in the context. Experiments with four LLMs (Qwen3-1.7B/4B-Base, Llama-3.2-1B/3B-Instruct) show that ASH consistently improves pass@$k$ on competition-level mathematics benchmarks (AMC, OlympiadBench, AIME24, AIME25) and out-of-distribution benchmarks (Minerva, GPQA-Diamond). Notably, it improves average pass@8 of Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Base by \textbf{2.60}\% and \textbf{2.21}\%.

authors.name: Ting Hua
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: Training Neural Networks to be Locally Adaptive
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks fitted by global empirical risk minimization commit to a single model for the entire covariate space. In a regression problem, if the regression function $f_0$ is inhomogeneous --- varying rapidly in one region, while being nearly flat in another --- no single model can be appropriate everywhere, and the fit degrades where the function varies most rapidly. Here we study an alternative in which, instead of fitting the network globally, we fit it locally. For each query point $x$, a \emph{local neural network} is trained on the $k$ nearest-neighbours of $x$ alone, making the training sample and the fitted function query-dependent. We analyze the performance of the resulting estimator through a localization approach, establishing that the pointwise risk of the estimator with an appropriate choice of $k$ attains the rate $n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+d^{*})}$, up to logarithmic factors, when $f_0$ is locally $\alpha$-H\"older with $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and the covariates are supported on a $d^{*}$-dimensional manifold embedded in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. A matching Le Cam lower bound shows that this rate is pointwise minimax optimal. However, the local rate-optimality requires $k$ to be calibrated to the smoothness of $f_0$, which is unknown in practice. We therefore provide a locally adaptive choice of $k$ that makes the neural network adapt to the local H\"older exponent of $f_0$ and to the intrinsic dimension simultaneously, both of which are potentially varying over the covariate domain. An extensive simulation study demonstrates the dominance of the locally adaptive neural network over a globally trained network and several state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Evolving Neural Solvers for Multi-objective Combinatorial Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-objective combinatorial optimization (MOCO) seeks high-quality solutions that represent different trade-offs among conflicting objectives. Existing neural methods typically train a dedicated model for each preference or condition a single model on different preferences. Training dedicated models becomes more costly as the number of preferences increases, while a shared model can produce duplicate solutions for different preferences, limiting the benefit of denser preference queries. We propose the Evolving Neural Solver (ENS), which trains only a small set of preference-specific models and takes advantage of evolutionary computation to evolve them into a diverse collection of solvers for better solution quality and Pareto front coverage. ENS first trains a model at an estimated knee-point preference to target a balanced compromise, then obtains the remaining initial models through parameter transfer toward the extremes, so as to preliminarily approximate the Pareto front. It then evolves these models to find more candidates that can generate non-dominated solutions through evolution strategies. Experimental results on classic MOCO problems show that ENS outperforms state-of-the-art neural MOCO methods in terms of hypervolume in most evaluated settings.

authors.name: Le-Xin Wen
authors.institution: Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Peoples Hospital

papers.title: RoadAnnoter: An AI-Assisted Desktop Tool for Semantic Segmentation Annotation of Road-Scene Images
papers.abstract: Accurate semantic segmentation of road-scene images is essential for road safety research; however, polygon-level annotation remains labor-intensive and limits labelled dataset development. This study presents RoadAnnoter v1.0, an open-source desktop application integrating six human-in-the-loop annotation modes: manual polygon delineation, SAM Prompt, Smart Select, Edge Fill, pretrained semantic segmentation using Cityscapes-trained SegFormer models, and task-specific segmentation using TinySegNet, a lightweight MobileNetV3-Small-based network trained with accumulated annotator-generated labels. SAM-based modes use promptable segmentation with SAM and MobileSAM, while Edge Fill combines Canny edge detection with colour-similarity-based flood filling in CIELAB colour space. SegFormer generates suggestions for common road-scene categories, whereas TinySegNet supports adaptation to project-specific features through iterative training. All six modes use a shared mask-to-polygon pipeline comprising morphological processing, Gaussian smoothing, contour extraction, and Douglas-Peucker simplification; annotations are exported in YOLO segmentation format. RoadAnnoter was used to annotate Google Street View images from recorded road accident locations in Bangladesh for a vision-language model-based investigation of free-flow speed estimation. Qualitative assessment across representative scenes demonstrated the complementary applicability of the annotation modes to diverse feature geometries. Visual comparison with Roboflow indicated similar qualitative boundary characteristics for principal road-scene regions, although no quantitative accuracy assessment was conducted. RoadAnnoter provides a locally operated framework for developing road-scene segmentation datasets for transportation engineering and road safety research.

papers.title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
papers.abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $\theta(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{\theta(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

papers.title: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
papers.abstract: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$.

authors.name: Yongheng Han
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: CEVA: Complementary Evidence Verification via Frame-Level Reorganization for Short-Video Fake News Detection
papers.abstract: Short-video platforms are now a common way for the public to follow unfolding events. Their rapid, visually persuasive format also makes fake news easier to spread. Unlike text-image posts, short-video news interleaves multiple modalities and changing scenes, making it difficult to identify which frames verify a claim. Existing detectors either pool sampled frames homogeneously or select them by text-frame similarity. Both overlook that aligned frames may repeat a misleading claim, whereas less dominant context may challenge it. We present CEVA (Complementary Evidence Verification Approach), to our knowledge the first short-video fake news detection framework to explicitly organize frames by their evidential roles before multimodal fusion. Its Dual-Branch Complementary Reorganization (DBCR) module separates explicit-alignment frames from candidate complementary-context frames, and cross-modal fusion with bidirectional contrastive regularization operates on the reorganized evidence. On FakeSV and FakeTT, CEVA achieves the best overall results among the compared methods. Under fixed frame budgets and backbones, DBCR outperforms uniform, random, and similarity-based selection and improves two structurally different detectors. Together, these results establish pre-fusion evidence organization as an effective and transferable component of short-video fake news detection.

authors.name: Jing Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

authors.name: Shuyu Jiang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: On the uniqueness of ground states for pseudo-relativistic boson stars
papers.abstract: We establish the uniqueness of both action and energy ground states for the pseudo-relativistic Hartree equation. The latter, for every prescribed mass below the critical stellar mass, proves the Lieb-Yau conjecture. Our approach establishes radial nondegeneracy and a strict monotonicity property of the mass-frequency relation, providing a unified framework for proving uniqueness in both variational settings.

papers.title: Grid-Responsive Pricing of Dynamic Wireless Charging with Coupled Residential Demand
papers.abstract: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) is an emerging technology that enables electric vehicles (EVs) to recharge while traveling. Its unique operational model creates two revenue streams for DWC operators through lane access tolls and electricity sales. However, these prices influence not only traffic flow and roadway energy delivery but also how much EV charging moves to homes instead, potentially within the same distribution network. Neglecting this coupling can underestimate grid loading and compromise pricing decisions. We develop a coupled traffic, EV energy, driver-response, and AC distribution network model with a model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes DWC tolls and charging prices while explicitly accounting for displaced residential charging and network losses. Using 78 days of I-210 West traffic data, we show that conventional MPC exceeds feeder loading limits on 52 days, whereas the proposed residential load aware controller eliminates these violations with only 0.6% lower operator revenue. Under a more constrained feeder configuration, it eliminates 50 overloaded days with a 0.9% revenue reduction. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of accurate residential demand estimation and feeder loss modeling, while peak-aware pricing further reduces daily peak loading by 3.7% relative to the base load. These results demonstrate the value of coordinated pricing that captures the interaction between roadway and residential charging.

authors.name: Dipanjan Ghose
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: FieldGuide: A Corpus Map for Token-Efficient Agentic Document Exploration
papers.abstract: Generative AI agents can help journalists explore large document collections. But exploratory workflows can require substantial token use and time, especially when the task is broad and the relevant subquestions are not yet known. This paper introduces FieldGuide, an agent-facing corpus map that organizes a document collection into a topic hierarchy and exposes tools for corpus orientation, scoped search, and bounded reading. I evaluate FieldGuide on five journalistic document-exploration tasks using 38 Chicago Police Department public-records documents, comparing it with raw-file access and retrieval-augmented generation. Across the five tasks, FieldGuide used 27% fewer tokens and 41% less elapsed time than raw-file access; relative to RAG, it used 38% fewer tokens and 21% less elapsed time. An accuracy audit identified four minor issues in FieldGuide's responses, comparable to the other conditions. In blind ratings of generated reporting leads, FieldGuide's mean ratings were higher than RAG's and lower than the raw-file condition's. These descriptive results suggest that corpus orientation may reduce runtime token use and elapsed time without severe accuracy failures. They also motivate further study of whether selective access limits broad, cross-document discovery.

papers.title: CRA: Continuous Risk Assessment for Safety-critical Visual Navigation
papers.abstract: Traditional safety-critical control methods often rely on predefined constraints that separate states into safe and unsafe regions. While recent studies have extended geometric safety toward semantic safety, real-world safety is rarely purely binary. The risk associated with an object or human can vary continuously with its physical properties, like motion, and interaction context; for example, a person carrying a heavy object or a hot object moving at high speed may require a different safety response from an ordinary static obstacle. In this paper, we propose a vision-based continuous risk assessment framework for safety-critical visual navigation. Our method uses RGB and LiDAR observations to estimate four risk factors (kinetic, potential, contact-severity, and thermal) and combines them into a continuous risk score for each assessed object or person. These estimates are integrated into a Poisson safety function with a Laplace guidance field as a safety filter, enabling online monitoring and intervention in open-world robot navigation. We demonstrate the proposed method in a simulated restaurant scene.

authors.name: Ying Wu
authors.institution: National Clinical Research Center for Digestive Diseases

papers.title: Where Does Hindsight Enter Clinical Agent Benchmarks? An Audit of Simulators and Case Construction
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for LLM diagnostic agents are built from retrospective records: the case an agent reads is rewritten from discharge summaries, and unrecorded test results are generated by a simulator that often sees the final diagnosis. HindAudit separates three hindsight channels (the diagnosis given to the simulator, the retrospective context it conditions on, and the agent-facing case text) and measures each with judges trained only on real data. On 27,489 emergency admissions from MIMIC-IV, five registered tests found no leakage into simulated laboratory results: providing the diagnosis to five simulators had a negligible effect, and prompted gatekeepers diluted the diagnostic signal, although exploratory results suggest they can raise agent scores. The largest effect lay in the case text. Against a presentation-time reconstruction from triage records, benchmark-style summaries raised the zero-shot accuracy of four LLMs from 25.4% to 39.7% and discharge histories to 45.3%, and raised six interactive agents' scores while barely changing their ranking. The exploratory gap was reproduced in a registered replication on held-out patients. Masking diagnosis names left it unchanged. Because MIMIC lacks a contemporaneous bedside history, the gap is an upper bound on hindsight. We report all registered outcomes and recommend construction practices.

papers.title: Nonlinear syzygies in ordinary powers of chordal cover ideals
papers.abstract: We construct connected chordal graphs whose cover ideals have ordinary powers that are not componentwise linear over any field, disproving the Herzog--Hibi--Ohsugi conjecture.

papers.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
papers.abstract: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them. Across seven evolution methods and six models (over 10M LLM calls), we find support for the hypothesis at both levels where evaluation scores are used. At the candidate level (choosing artifacts), helpful candidate artifacts exist, but selection is no better than random at telling them from harmful ones, so errors accumulate across rounds. At the method level (ranking methods), typical margins of a few percentage points are smaller than the difference between two independent runs of the same method, so published rankings often rest on luck. Together, these findings indicate that agent evolution is often bottlenecked by reliably identifying improvements. This calls for a shift in how we develop and evaluate self-improving agents, from designing ever more candidate improvement systems to making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

authors.name: Kuang Yan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Kan Ren
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: EviSlide-MIL: Multi-Query Pooling and Shared Prediction for Class-Incremental Whole-Slide Image Classification
papers.abstract: Histopathological analysis of whole-slide images (WSIs) plays a critical role in cancer diagnosis, and multiple instance learning (MIL) is widely adopted for WSI analysis under weak supervision. As new tumor subtypes are introduced, extending existing MIL models requires learning new classes while retaining knowledge of previously learned ones. This presents a class-incremental learning challenge, where models must acquire new classes with limited access to historical training data and recognize all learned classes without task identifiers at inference. A major obstacle is forgetting, as updates to feature aggregation and prediction modules can degrade performance on previously learned classes. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{EviSlide-MIL}, a class-incremental WSI framework that integrates multiple learnable queries per class with a shared prediction module. The queries aggregate frozen patch features into class-specific representations, while the shared prediction module limits parameter growth across incremental stages. By freezing queries associated with previously learned classes, EviSlide-MIL preserves their attention patterns for identical inputs, while experience replay and knowledge distillation further mitigate forgetting as shared parameters are updated. Experiments on eight tumor subtypes from The Cancer Genome Atlas demonstrate that EviSlide-MIL achieves improved performance and reduced forgetting compared with competing methods across most learning settings, demonstrating its potential for scalable and knowledge-preserving WSI classification. Code and pretrained models will be released.

papers.title: Strong Fused Performance Can Mask Branch Collapse in a Dual-View Heart-Sound Classifier: A Three-Part Diagnostic Protocol
papers.abstract: Fusion models are usually judged by their fused score, a practice that assumes that every branch has learned something useful. We show that this assumption can fail silently in dual-view heart-sound classification. In AudioFuse, which fuses a spectrogram transformer with a waveform CNN, the spectrogram branch is unused despite strong fused performance when both branches are trained from scratch. We introduce a three-part diagnostic for branch collapse: whether deleting a branch changes the fused score, whether a linear probe on its features beats an untrained copy of the same branch, and whether the branch can learn its view when trained alone. Deleting the branch has negligible effect, and probing its features shows little improvement over an identically initialised, untrained copy. Yet the same architecture trained alone exceeds 0.9 AUC, so its view is learnable, while the jointly trained model is near chance when it must rely on this branch. Update statistics and an initialisation experiment point to an early optimisation imbalance. Moving a strong artificial label cue from one input to the other can switch which branch the model relies on, even though the branch architectures stay the same. We observe branch collapse on PhysioNet, but the full diagnostic is not met on ICBHI or CirCor. Fused performance alone therefore cannot establish that every branch learned a meaningful representation, and we recommend reporting branch deletion and an untrained-control probe alongside it.

papers.title: RTLReviewBench: LLM Hardware Reviewers Rarely Miss Bugs but Routinely Reject Correct RTL
papers.abstract: Hardware teams increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) to review register-transfer level (RTL) code, yet it is unclear whether a model can tell a correct module from a buggy one without simulating it. We introduce RTLReviewBench, a benchmark of 114 matched pairs of buggy and correct Verilog modules. Each pair shares one specification, most buggy modules are real failures of LLM code generators, and every label is confirmed by simulation. Evaluating 12 commercial and open-weight models, we find a consistent asymmetry: reviewers rarely accept buggy code but often reject correct code, producing more than five false rejections for every missed bug. Synthetic mutants hide part of the problem: on the same designs, models miss far fewer injected bugs than real ones. Asking a model to reason before it commits to a verdict sharply reduces false rejections for weaker reviewers, and a controlled ablation shows that where the reasoning appears in the output matters more than the instruction to reason, whereas sampling and majority voting do not help. A blinded audit further shows that some correct "buggy" verdicts rest on false technical claims. We release the benchmark, a harder split for future models, all model responses, and the evaluation code at https://github.com/yasirmahmud/RTLReviewBench

authors.name: Yasir Mahmud
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: PS-HalluBench: Taxonomy-Driven Benchmarking of LLM Hallucinations in Power Systems
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for power-system applications, yet their reliability in engineering analysis remains uncertain. We introduce PS-HalluBench, a manually constructed benchmark of 200 questions that evaluates hallucination-related failures across five power-system task categories: numerical reasoning, network topology, constraint verification, false-premise acceptance, and abstention. We evaluate ten LLMs over the benchmark, yielding 39.35\% overall correctness, with constraint verification achieving only 21.75\%, and highlighting persistent difficulties in engineering reasoning. We further investigate engineering-grounded reasoning through numerical solver support and verified network information both of which show significant performance improvement. The findings reveal important limitations of standalone LLM reasoning and motivate integrating LLMs with verified engineering tools for reliable power-system analysis.

authors.name: S. M. Monzurul Hoque Chowdhury
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: An Explainable Agentic AI Framework for Distribution System Load Restoration
papers.abstract: Distribution system load restoration is a sequential decision-making problem in which restoration actions must maximize served load, prioritize critical loads, and preserve power-flow feasibility. This paper proposes an explainable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for distribution system load restoration. The proposed framework uses multiple large language model (LLM) agents for planner guidance, strategic plan generation, decision arbitration, memory-based feedback, and explanation generation. Unlike unconstrained LLM-based control, the proposed method restricts agent decisions to feasible restoration actions and evaluates all candidate plans using deterministic AC power-flow feasibility checks. The framework is evaluated on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus distribution feeders, as well as a larger IEEE 118-bus test case, and compared against reinforcement learning and planning baselines. The results show that the proposed agentic framework achieves better restoration performance while producing structured explanations for operator-facing decision support. A direct comparison with a Single-LLM-Agent baseline further shows that the proposed multi-agent decomposition improves weighted restored load and critical-load recovery compared with a monolithic LLM decision structure.

authors.name: S. M. Monzurul Hoque Chowdhury
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
papers.abstract: We develop neural network methods for the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations at a small viscosity $\varepsilon > 0$, whose accuracy is uniform in $\varepsilon$ and whose residual is evaluated on a grid that does not resolve the vorticity boundary layer. In the vorticity-stream function formulation with the slip boundary conditions, a vorticity layer of width $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ forms along the walls. The trial function of the singular layer Physics-Informed Neural Network (sl-PINN) contains the corrector of the asymptotic analysis, together with the law that fixes its amplitude at the wall. The amplitude is tied to the wall trace of the network itself, so that the method requires no a priori knowledge of the limit solution. The sl-PINN keeps the error uniform in $\varepsilon$ over six decades, for the Stokes and the Navier-Stokes equations alike, although in the latter the wall trace travels with the flow and is not known in advance. An enrichment that uses the thin scale but leaves the profile and the amplitude of the layer free deteriorates as $\varepsilon\to0$. Since the corrector carries the layer analytically, the Laplacian in the residual can be discretized by a finite volume flux difference on a coarse grid. The resulting singular layer Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) attains the same uniform accuracy as the sl-PINN, to within the scatter of the random seed, at about half the cost of a training step. The combination of the asymptotic corrector with the coarse-grid finite volume discretization is the main result of this article.

authors.name: Chang-Yeol Jung
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Missing Security-Fix Backporting for GitHub Actions Workflows
papers.abstract: GitHub natively supports workflow automation through GitHub Actions, now the dominant CI/CD tool on the platform. Yet keeping these workflows secure remains an ongoing burden: maintainers often patch a vulnerability on the default branch but leave the same flaw on the release and maintenance branches that downstream consumers continue to build from. Carrying a known fix onto these divergent branches, called backporting, is rarely done, and this paper presents the first large-scale empirical study quantifying the resulting gap. From a public corpus of GitHub Actions workflow histories, we mine 1,903,191 workflow-modifying commits, scan each before and after with the static scanner zizmor to identify 69,865 security fixes across 24,238 projects, and audit every release branch to check whether each fix was carried over. The gap is pervasive: 224,392 of 474,490 audited release branches remain vulnerable, and deliberate backporting is rare and slow, with only 19,476 of 78,907 already-fixed branches confirmed as plausible backports at a median lag of 243 days. We thus design WorkflowBP, the first technique for automated security-fix backporting of GitHub Actions workflows. WorkflowBP takes a neuro-symbolic approach: it compiles a default-branch fix into a domain-specific representation called the Workflow Semantic Patch (WSP) and applies it to each divergent branch by matching jobs and steps based on their content rather than their position, while an LLM synthesizes the WSP for the most divergent cases the deterministic engine cannot resolve. On 12,000 real unpatched workflow files from our study, WorkflowBP produces a scanner-checked backport for 67.9%. We further submit 176 issues with WorkflowBP-generated backports to real-world projects, 44 of which have been confirmed or fixed by developers.

papers.title: Beyond the Camera: A Tri-Modal Driving World Model for Future RGB, Thermal, and LiDAR Forecasting in Adverse Weather
papers.abstract: Driving world models forecast what a vehicle's sensors will record next. Most forecast camera video and some add LiDAR, but thermal cameras, which still see in darkness and some adverse weather, are rarely a forecast target, and to our knowledge no world model forecasts all three sensors. We study joint forecasting of RGB, thermal, and LiDAR on real adverse-weather sequences of the DSERT-RoLL dataset. We post-train a pretrained video world model for each sensor and represent LiDAR as a depth video aligned with the RGB camera, with densification and encoding chosen by what the model's video tokenizer can reconstruct. A tri-sensor model sees all three sensors as one video. We score LiDAR in meters against measured returns and compare against persistence baselines passed through the same tokenizer as the model. With this matching, an apparent loss of the thermal model to persistence in fog disappears. On all 58 validation sequences in six weather conditions, post-trained RGB and thermal forecasts beat compression-matched persistence. Joint training lowers the LiDAR error at 2s by 2.1m at a small cost in camera fidelity, and only the tri-sensor model's LiDAR forecasts beat persistence in mean error. Blanking one sensor degrades the forecasts of the others more in snow than in fog.

authors.name: Md. Mahfuzur Rahman
authors.institution: Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

papers.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
papers.abstract: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $\rho = -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $\phi = 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.

affiliations.raw: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Dhaka
affiliations.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.intro:
A growing family of methods localises social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and mitigates it by ablating them (Han et al., 2026; Jahan, 2026; Zayed et al., 2023; Islam et al., 2026; Yang et al., 2023). The statistics differ in kind but the structure is shared: a per-head score induces a ranking, a selection rule turns it into a set, and the set is zeroed. Most members compute their statistic on minimal pairs or at a single token position, where the two conditions contrasted are matched by construction. A newer design instead elicits free-form responses under two prompting conditions, labels each fair or unfair with a judge, and computes the statistic separately over each label set (Han et al., 2026). We audit that design in depth and ask a question that applies to the family as a whole: what does a head-attribution statistic for social bias actually measure, and what does ablating its output actually do?

A growing family of methods localises social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and mitigates it by ablating them (Han et al., 2026; Jahan, 2026; Zayed et al., 2023; Islam et al., 2026; Yang et al., 2023). The statistics differ in kind but the structure is shared: a per-head score induces a ranking, a selection rule turns it into a set, and the set is zeroed. Most members compute their statistic on minimal pairs or at a single token position, where the two conditions contrasted are matched by construction. A newer design instead elicits free-form responses under two prompting conditions, labels each fair or unfair with a judge, and computes the statistic separately over each label set (Han et al., 2026). We audit that design in depth and ask a question that applies to the family as a whole: what does a head-attribution statistic for social bias actually measure, and what does ablating its output actually do?

We reproduce the paradigm on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The first result appears to be a clean answer. A control map built from the same per-example scores under an explicit alternative hypothesis — response length, ignoring fairness labels entirely — correlates at −0.950-0.950 with the fairness map on Qwen and −0.768-0.768 on Llama, with nine and eight of the ten top-ranked heads among each model’s ten most length-suppressed. Four further controls agree, and the correlation strengthens as the adversarial persona is weakened. A mechanism is available: committing to a group is terse and declining is verbose.

Every piece of that evidence is correlational, and it is wrong. We test this through an intervention. We ask the same questions using prompts that encourage either verbose or brief responses, filling the long-unfair and short-fair combinations missing from the original data. We keep the identified heads fixed throughout. Within a single prompt the heads do not track length. In the terse condition, where responses average just ten tokens, length explains 1% of the statistic’s variance while its correlation with the fairness label is +0.690+0.690 (Section 4.4). The pooled correlation was a between-arm artifact. What dominates the score is prompt identity: arm membership alone explains 64% of variance, in an ordering not monotonic in length. The construct itself proves unidentifiable — within a fixed prompt the fairness label and the presence of a protected-group token are the same variable (ϕ=0.95\phi=0.95), one direction of which is entailed by the labelling rule. No observational analysis distinguishes them, and no method in this family runs an experiment that would.

Contributions. (1) A correlational control that misleads and the intervention that catches it (Sections 4.3–4.4): the diagnostic this literature lacks returned −0.950-0.950 for a hypothesis an intervention subsequently rejected, and every further correlational control agreed with it. (2) Two non-reproductions with quantified uncertainty, and the positive control that licenses them (Sections 4.5–4.6): bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated against a ten-draw layer-matched null, while its complement reliably destroys refusal behaviour and replicates across near-disjoint reselections (p=1.75×10−5p=1.75\times 10^{-5}), the control Kendiukhov (2026) identifies as missing from ablation-based audits. papers.title: SE(3)-LIVOM: Adaptive Multi-LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry and Mapping
papers.abstract: This paper presents SE(3)-LIVOM, the overall winner of the COMFORT Challenge at IROS 2026. The challenge asks for the trajectory of a legged robot in the GrandTour dataset, whose scenes include collapsed buildings, construction sites and snowfields. SE(3)-LIVOM runs in real time on two LiDARs, one camera and an IMU. Its frontend extends SE(3)-LIO to multiple LiDARs and a camera. Adaptive downsampling keeps the time per scan near 35 ms within and across scenes. An online backend corrects drift with a plane bundle adjustment over submaps and an incremental pose graph. With a single configuration for all scenes, the system reaches an average ATE of 1.40 cm on the six test scenes. The code is available at https://github.com/url-kaist/se3-livom-comfort.

papers.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. Our new cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline converts existing RGB videos into demonstrations for alternative embodiments by retargeting the recovered motion and synthesizing the corresponding observations, without recorded source-robot states. Experiments show that the tracker achieves absolute trajectory errors of 7.60 and 16.07 mm on DROID and RoboLab and adapts to a new embodiment with only ten demonstrations. The generator achieves 69.19% mean success on RoboTwin and outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks, while joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.

papers.title: PCGRL for Complex Platformers: Synthesizing Playable and Diverse Levels via Inflated Envelopes and Forward Curricula
papers.abstract: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning (PCGRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for automated game development. However, existing PCGRL frameworks still suffer from severe exploration bottlenecks and scaling limitations when faced with long-sequence generation tasks governed by strict rigid-body rules and non-linear kinematic boundaries (e.g., platformer constraints). Consequently, traditional approaches frequently fail to maintain reliable level solvability on large-scale canvases. To address these challenges, we present a physics-aware, curriculum-guided PCGRL framework. First, we construct an "Inflated Volume Envelope" mechanism, which provides a physics-constrained representation that incorporates continuous kinematic feasibility into the discrete state space of the MDP. Second, to alleviate the sparse reward challenge induced by extremely long decision sequences, we introduce intermediate state-transition feedback and a multi-stage forward extension curriculum learning framework, enabling informative value estimation and stable credit assignment over long-horizon trajectories. Finally, to resolve the issue where deterministic policies after convergence generate highly monotonous map paths with a lack of diversity, we activate high-entropy stochastic inference during the synthesis phase, regularized by a post-hoc parallel rejection filtering mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances structural diversity while maintaining high physical playability across multi-scale environments. Comparative evaluations across multi-scale canvases demonstrate that our framework maintains superior convergence stability and dimensional scalability, reliably synthesizing solvable levels where traditional PCGRL baselines degrade.

authors.name: Di Wu
authors.institution: Lanzhou Institute of Husbandry and Pharmaceutical Sciences

papers.title: Finite element nonlinear nudging for the Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: Nonlinear nudging augments the classical linear nudging (continuous data as- similation) term with a nonlinear feedback that strengthens as the observed error decreases, and yields super-exponential convergence to the true state. In this paper, we study nonlinear nudging for the 3-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the finite element method, which allows complex geometries and physical boundary conditions. We propose an implicit-explicit (IMEX) finite element scheme with inf-sup stable elements, prove its unconditional long-time stability, and show for the spatially semi-discrete scheme that the error reaches a prescribed tolerance in finite time. Our analysis also suggests that the non- linear nudging term requires the mesh resolution to be fine enough (${\chi = O(H^{-1})}$, where ${\chi}$ is the nonlinear nudging intensity and ${H}$ is the observation mesh size). Further, our error estimates suggest that a larger nonlinear exponent ${\gamma}$ requires finer observational resolution, which is confirmed by numerical tests. Numerical experiments, including two-dimensional forced viscous flow in a periodic box, flow past a cylinder, and flow over a flat plate, show that nonlinear nudging synchronizes with the true solution considerably faster than linear nudging. We also show that observations in a subregion suffice to synchronize the whole flow

papers.title: Fold Weighting for Cross-Validation Under Continuous Distributional Drift
papers.abstract: Cross-validation weights all folds equally, so under drift the oldest folds count as much as the newest. We model drift by a H\"older condition in total variation distance and give finite-sample bounds on the excess deployment risk of the configuration that sliding-window cross-validation selects. Each bound splits into drift, estimation, and validation-noise terms. With equal weights the drift terms saturate as the record grows. With fold weights fixed in advance, the drift terms become weighted averages, which shrink as weight moves toward deployment. The noise term grows as the weights concentrate and shrinks with the batch size. The drift terms are linear in the weights and the noise term is convex, so minimizing the bound over the weights is a convex problem. Applications to U.S. earnings and flight delays show both sides of this trade-off. Weight on recent folds pays off when a change in the best predictor persists and each period has many observations, and equal weights do best when changes are short-lived.

papers.title: Quantum Interband-Coherence-Driven Inverse Faraday Effect in Intrinsic Graphene
papers.abstract: The inverse Faraday effect converts the angular momentum of circularly polarized light into a quasistatic magnetization, providing a fundamental route to ultrafast optical control of magnetic fields. We develop an analytical quantum theory of this effect in intrinsic graphene, where massless Dirac fermions, electron-hole symmetry, and weak spin-orbit coupling suppress conventional population-based interpretations. We show that in intrinsic graphene, the helicity-dependent orbital magnetization arises from the off-diagonal zero-harmonic component of the second-order density matrix, rather than from intraband carrier circulation or diagonal population imbalance. We obtain closed expressions for the induced temporal surface magnetization, its finite-pulse dynamics, and the nonlocal stray magnetic field generated by the two-dimensional (2D) source. Optical helicity, frequency, pulse envelope, and beam profile independently control the response. Our results identify intrinsic graphene as an ideal platform for coherent orbital optomagnetism in 2D Dirac matter.
