papers.title: Normalized solutions for logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equations on graphs
papers.abstract: We study a logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equation with prescribed $L^2$ mass on connected locally finite weighted graphs, with $p > 2$. By minimizing the energy, we obtain a positive solution for every prescribed mass $m > 0$ on finite graphs and, under additional assumptions on the vertex measure and the potential, on infinite graphs. We describe the behavior of positive solutions and their Lagrange multipliers as $m \to 0^+$ or $m \to +\infty$. In particular, as $m \to 0^+$, the minimizers rescaled to unit mass converge along subsequences to functions supported at a single vertex.

papers.title: MARS: Feature-guided physics-informed deep learning for real-time battery health and lifetime prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate and robust estimation of battery state-of-health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) is essential for safe and cost-effective operation of electrified transportation systems, yet it remains challenging under operating variability, non-stationary aging, and non-Gaussian measurement disturbances. This paper proposes Multi-scale Adaptive Robust State Estimation (MARS), a multi-scale adaptive robust state-estimation framework that couples a dual-branch temporal encoder with an equivalent-circuit-model-constrained differentiable generalized-correntropy adaptive Kalman filter. The encoder disentangles fast intra-cycle voltage-current-temperature dynamics from slow inter-cycle degradation, and the fused degradation context adaptively parameterizes the cycle-level process covariance, measurement covariance, and correntropy bandwidth. Through the unrolled robust filtering recursion, MARS performs physics-consistent state propagation and generalized-correntropy-based innovation correction, while uncertainty decomposition and Monte Carlo dropout provide calibrated prediction intervals for SOH estimation and conditional RUL prediction. Experiments on the NASA and CALCE benchmarks demonstrate improved SOH accuracy, achieving mean absolute error/root mean square error values of 0.72%/0.92% and 0.63%/0.80%, respectively, together with competitive conditional RUL performance against representative data-driven and hybrid baselines. The resulting conditional-RUL prediction intervals achieve coverage probabilities of 100.00% and 99.24% on NASA and CALCE, respectively. Ablation, disturbance-sensitivity, near-end-of-life, and runtime analyses further verify the contribution of each module and the practical inference cost for online battery management.

papers.title: Growing Clusters Lower the Bar: Profile Accretion in LLM-Based Incremental Entity Resolution
papers.abstract: Incremental entity resolution pipelines ask a large language model (LLM) whether a new record belongs to an existing cluster and show it the records already linked. Analyses of matching oracles assume that the answer depends only on the records compared. For the LLM matchers we test, it depends on cluster size, and the model lowers its bar for joining a cluster as the cluster grows. On French procurement suppliers from FOPPA, with SIREN identifiers as ground truth, we hold the new record fixed and vary only the number of verified members shown. Sixteen members instead of one raise the false match rate on similarly named companies by \dfmrMin--\dfmrMax{} percentage points in six open-weight models, while their area under the ROC curve rises by only \aucGainMin--\aucGainMax. In Claude Sonnet~5 and Haiku~5.5 the rise is \clSonD{} and \clHaiD{} points. The shift persists with street addresses, prompt variants and the BatchER and ComEM formats, and one false merge raises acceptance of the intruder's other records in every open model. It does not arise on Czech and Bulgarian TED notices, where one record with its full address already identifies the company. In online linking on confusable blocks, a single threshold set on labelled data raises recall by a factor of \fxRRmin--\fxRRmax{} for five models with no detectable loss of precision and no extra LLM calls.

authors.name: Huixue Han
authors.institution: National Health and Family Planning Commission

papers.title: The Multivariate Feedback Particle Filter for State-dependent Multiplicative Noises and Its Application to Attitude and Pose Estimations
papers.abstract: Nonlinear filtering with state-dependent multiplicative measurement noise poses a notable challenge for spacecraft attitude determination and robotic pose estimation. This work develops the FPF-DM, a decomposition scheme for feedback particle filters tailored to this family of filtering problems. Extending prior decomposition techniques for additive noise and polynomial measurement models, the proposed method resolves the key difficulty that state-dependent multiplicative noise breaks the polynomial assumption and prevents Hermite spectral backward recursion for the weighted Poisson's equation. By measure transformation and importance reweighting, we incorporate the inverse measurement covariance into particle weights and rescale the feedback gain to restore the polynomial-form Poisson's equation, with the decomposition generalized to non-uniformly weighted mixtures for closed-form gain computation. This general FPF-DM is instantiated on quaternion and dual-quaternion manifolds for attitude tracking and point-cloud registration. Simulations on 4D attitude tracking and 8D point-cloud registration verify that the instantiated filters using only 10 particles achieve superior accuracy and computational performance relative to baseline filters.

papers.title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
papers.abstract: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calder\'on--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

authors.name: Fan Bu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Hausdorff reflections and obstruction ideals for filter topologies on MV-algebras
papers.abstract: MV-algebras arise in many-valued logic and are closely related to lattice-ordered groups. We characterize Hausdorff separation in filter topologies through their associated ideals. For every proper lattice filter, $T_0$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ are equivalent, and the zero-neighborhood ideal determines a canonical Hausdorff reflection. For a radius filter satisfying a refinement condition, the filter topology agrees with the ambient subspace topology exactly when every radius is a weak order unit. This answers a question of Luan, Zhao and Yang without requiring divisibility of the representing group. These results reveal two successive algebraic obstructions: a polar obstruction controlling compatibility with the ambient topology, followed by a relative infinitesimal obstruction controlling the residual failure of Hausdorff separation. For a unital lattice-ordered subring of $C(X,\mathbb R)$, where $X$ is compact Hausdorff and the unit is $\mathbf1$, the associated exact sequence admits a positive additive section exactly when the relative infinitesimal ideal vanishes.

authors.name: Yanyan Dong
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing
papers.abstract: Instruction-driven image editors produce convincing local edits in one pass, but inside an iterative refinement loop every accepted output becomes the next input, so unintended changes outside the requested region accumulate. We present ConserveEdit, an editor-agnostic controller that treats each refinement step as a transaction against a contract compiled once from the source image. The contract separates what may change (the authorized region of each target, with a bounded halo for shadows and reflections) from what must survive (protected content with explicit tolerances). Candidates from a frozen editor are composed through a source-anchored mask and committed only if target progress, drift on protected content, and image quality pass as separate tests; otherwise the step is rolled back and repaired. For any editor, this keeps every pixel outside the authorized region bit-exact and bounds drift independently of the number of iterations, whereas no fixed scalar trade-off reproduces the separate tests. On all 1053 MagicBrush test edits with a frozen Qwen-Image-Edit, masking is necessary but not sufficient. A direct call already alters the rest of the image (12.1 dB PSNR outside the mask); composed through the source-anchored mask, it stays bit-exact there and its DINO similarity to the ground truth rises from 0.67 to 0.85, matching ConserveEdit, so this gain comes from the mask. Next to automatic masks, however, masked direct editing changes a protected face or text on 48% of turns, and masked scalar selection avoids this mostly by abstaining (23% constrained success). Because its drift test names the violated entity, ConserveEdit shrinks the support instead (2% violations, 53% constrained success); in a simulator with known ground truth it raises constrained success from 55.0% to 61.8%. Automatic grounding remains the main bottleneck. Code and logs will be released.

authors.name: Zhenyu Wu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SlopeGuard: Towards Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection via Radial Spectral Slope Guidance
papers.abstract: AI-generated image detectors often overfit to generator-specific artifacts, hindering generalization to unseen synthesis pipelines. Existing frequency-based methods usually learn high-dimensional spectral patterns that may preserve generator-dependent variations. We explore Radial Spectral Slope, a compact descriptor of global spectral decay that captures transferable spectral trends while suppressing fine-grained variations. Our analysis shows that real and generated images exhibit systematic but generator-dependent slope differences, indicating that slope provides useful forensic evidence but is insufficient as a standalone decision criterion. This motivates combining spectral slope with semantic representations for more robust detection. Based on this insight, we propose SlopeGuard, which couples slope-aware data processing with slope guided feature learning to construct informative patch-based views, integrate Radial Spectral Slope with semantic features, and adapt prior preservation according to spectral atypicality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SlopeGuard achieves state-of-the-art mean accuracies of 97.5% on AIGCDetectBench, 97.8% on GenImage, and 85.1% on AIGIBench, while maintaining competitive performance under blur, cropping, JPEG compression, and additive noise.

papers.title: Spin-Adapted Neural-Network Backflow Wavefunctions for Excited States of Strongly Correlated Open-Shell Systems
papers.abstract: Building on the success of neural-network quantum states (NQS) for molecular ground states, multi-state frameworks such as natural excited states (NES) [Pfau et al., Science 2024, 385, eadn0137] extend NQS to chemically important excited states. However, without control over total spin, such calculations can require the inclusion of many intervening states of other spins, particularly in strongly correlated systems with dense low-energy spectra. We therefore generalize our previously developed spin-adapted neural network backflow (SA-NNBF) ansatz [Li et al., arXiv:2604.06841 (2026)] to improve its variational flexibility for excited-state calculations within a prescribed spin sector. We establish the universality of this extended ansatz within the chosen orbital space and spin sector, and use numerical benchmarks to assess how parameter allocation affects the ansatz's accuracy. With the spin-adapted ansatz, we are able to directly optimize the first excited state (a singlet) of $O_2$ without using any multi-state frameworks. Combining the extended ansatz with NES, we obtain low-lying triplet states of $O_2$ and singlet states of the $[\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{S}_2(\mathrm{SCH}_3)_4]^{2-}$ cluster without including intervening states of other spins. Both the single-state and NES calculations achieve chemical accuracy relative to the exact energies. Our work provides a practical NQS framework for targeting excited states of prescribed spin in strongly correlated systems.

papers.title: Quantitative FS-domains over continuous t-norms
papers.abstract: We introduce quantitative FS-domains over continuous t-norms using a scalar-valued finite-separation degree and an approximate identity. The construction recovers classical FS-domains over the Boolean base. Symmetric quantitative FS-domains are characterized by compactness of their ball topology. In particular, a complete metric space is a quantitative FS-domain if and only if it is compact. Quantitative FS-domains are continuous and form a symmetric monoidal closed category under tensor products and function spaces of Yoneda-continuous maps. This category is Cartesian closed exactly for the G\"odel t-norm.

authors.name: Di Yang
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: Tilings of integer sets of prime-power cardinality
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite integer tile of cardinality $p^k$, where $p$ is prime and $k\geq1$. We first determine all possible fundamental periods of tilings of $A$. A cyclotomic argument gives a common period $PD$, where $P$ is a power of $p$ and $D$ is a greatest common divisor of normalized differences in $A$. Each $Pd$ with $d\mid D$ occurs as a fundamental period. At modulus $Pd$, a chain of greatest common divisors controls the compatibility of the Chinese remainder fibres. This yields independent digit functions and exact counts of the tilings. For tilings of fundamental period $Pd$, we classify their partitions into translates modulo $Pd$ and count the tilings that induce each partition. The same arithmetic data classify tiles with identical tiling families. Each class has a unique normalized tile of minimum diameter whose mask polynomial divides the masks of all normalized tiles in the class.

papers.title: A Neural Envelope Method for Rapid Gradient-based Optimum Takeoff Trajectory Design
papers.abstract: Urban air mobility arises to mitigate ground traffic congestion. Multidisciplinary analysis and optimization (MDAO) has been introduced to reduce the energy consumption, thereby expanding aircraft performance. Surrogate-based MDAO lowers the cost of optimization, but multimodality disrupts global optimum search for both simulation-based and surrogate-based optimizations. Convex envelopes convert multimodal spaces into unimodal spaces, permitting efficient convex optimization; however, convexifying a design space may produce infeasible "optimal" designs due to complex design constraints. To address these challenges, this work proposes the coupling of a physics-constrained generative adversarial networks (physicsGAN) and neural envelope to transform original, constrained, non-convex optimizations into unconstrained, convex optimizations. Specifically, the physicsGAN discovers a feasible design space where all design candidates inherently satisfy all constraints, by penalizing surrogate-predicted constraint violations during training. Moreover, the neural envelope constructs a neural network-based convex envelope for the transformed objective function within the physicsGAN-discovered feasible space. Note that the neural envelope only needs to deal with objective function since constraints are inherently satisfied in the feasible space. The neural envelope is demonstrated on takeoff trajectory optimizations of the Airbus A3 Vahana eVTOL aircraft. Results show that neural envelopes achieve a 99.91% mean accuracy within a flight-condition space compared with reference convex envelopes. Neural-envelope-enabled optimizations achieve 99.84% accuracy on the global optimum design, costing only 0.04 seconds on average. The neural envelope accelerates the trajectory optimization by 53 and 162 times on average compared to the physicsGAN-enabled gradient-based and global optimizations, respectively.

authors.name: Samuel Sisk
authors.institution: Missouri University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiaosong Du
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training
papers.abstract: Controlled studies of latent two-hop reasoning train transformers to predict only the answer, whereas language models are trained to predict every token. We ask whether a model trained on every token learns to answer two-hop questions whose intermediate entity appears in no two-hop training example. We build a synthetic corpus with such questions. On this corpus every term of the loss can be computed exactly. A looped transformer, a standard transformer and DiscoLoop answer almost none of these questions. We therefore introduce the Baton family of looped transformers. They pass the intermediate entity to the second loop as a token embedding. When trained to predict only the answer, two of its three variants answer these questions almost perfectly. We then relate the success and failure of each model to three design conditions. Experiments that change one condition at a time agree with this hypothesis. When Baton is trained on every token, however, its accuracy on these questions rises and then declines. We further split the gradient of the next-token loss into three terms. Removing the two terms that depend on the particular training set raises the peak accuracy but does not remove the decline. The decline arises in the second hop while the model still recalls both facts.

authors.name: Feiying Chen
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: DACE: Diversity-Driven Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robust LLM Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Ensuring robust safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly difficult as adversarial attacks evolve and outpace alignment pipelines built on pre-collected data. Existing co-evolutionary frameworks let the defender chase a moving attacker, yet their training dynamics expose two compounding pathologies: \emph{attack strategy collapse}, where the attacker overfits to a narrow set of high-reward rewrites, and \emph{defense adversarial forgetting}, where the defender loses competence against earlier attacks as the attack distribution drifts. Existing remedies are partial: attacker-side diversity rewards score textual novelty rather than strategy novelty, and defender-side replay relies on discrete judge scores that ignore estimation uncertainty, response stochasticity, and defender non-stationarity. We introduce \textbf{\method}, a diversity-driven adversarial co-evolution framework that targets both pathologies jointly. On the attacker side, \method couples an explicit two-dimensional strategy space (risk category $\times$ attack style) with a \emph{normalized marginal coverage gain} reward, providing a bounded, non-vanishing exploration signal at the strategy layer. On the defender side, \method maintains a unified \emph{Bayesian adversarial replay pool} whose Beta--Bernoulli threat posteriors are refreshed by time decay and sampled via Thompson sampling, anchoring defender training to an evolving threat landscape. Across standard safety, automated-attacker, and general-capability benchmarks, \method improves robustness to out-of-distribution attacks while preserving general capabilities, and yields broader attacker strategy coverage.

authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Ziyuan Zhou
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: A faster algorithm for commutator length in free groups
papers.abstract: We compute the commutator length $\cl(w)$ of a reduced word $w\in[F,F]$ of length $M$ in a free group. Given a target $g\ge1$, a deterministic algorithm decides $\cl(w)\le g$ and, when it holds, returns a decomposition into at most $g$ commutators, in $O(M^{3g})$ steps; trying $g=1,2,\dots$ gives $\cl(w)$ in $O(M^{3\cl(w)})$ steps. For $g=1$ the same test takes $O(M)$ expected steps on a uniformly random reduced input in $[F,F]$. All bounds are in the unit-cost model.

papers.title: Milk yield responses to heat stress in tropical dairy cattle
papers.abstract:
Context: Rising temperatures and warm tropical nights threaten dairy productivity and resilience across tropical landscapes.
  Objective: This study characterises multi-scale interactions among thermal regimes, nighttime cooling, metabolic heat load, and crossbred genetics on daily milk yield in Brazilian dairy systems.
  Methods: A 24-year panel (2001--2024) of 788,528 test-day records from 87,809 Girolando (Holstein $\times$ Gyr) cows across 408 municipalities was linked to weather data. Two-way fixed effects, distributed lag, and piecewise threshold spline models were estimated across yield quartiles and crossbred fractions.
  Results: While aggregate summaries suggest stable yield up to a daily mean Temperature--Humidity Index (THI) of 76, production-stratified splines show high-yielding cows lose milk starting at THI 68 and accelerating above 76 ($-0.162$ kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$ unit$^{-1}$, $p=0.0062$), whereas low-yielding cows remain unaffected ($p=0.81$). Distributed lag models reveal an immediate drop followed by a deeper trough four days later. Lack of nighttime relief ($\mathrm{THI}_{\min} \ge 68$) reduces yield by an extra 2.37 kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$ ($p \le 0.001$) and causes an 8.6\% loss after seven warm nights, whereas wide diurnal amplitude buffers output by $+1.60$ kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$. At comparable high yields ($\approx 31$ kg animal$^{-1}$ d$^{-1}$), intermediate crossbreds ($1/2$ and $5/8$ Holstein) sustain yield up to THI 76, whereas $7/8$ Holstein cows decline at THI 68.
  Conclusions: Tropical dairy adaptation requires continuous nighttime cooling for high-yielding cows combined with balanced Zebu--taurine crossbreeding.

authors.name: Marcos Vinicius Gualberto Barbosa da Silva

papers.title: Who Pays for Product Returns? Advertising and Return Policies
papers.abstract: An online marketplace decides how consumers, firms, and the platform share the cost of product returns. We study this decision when the platform earns commissions and sells prominent placement. Consumers inspect, try, and return products; firms bid for the first position and then set prices. Earlier display attracts more trials but can retain a smaller fraction of them. For small positive losses, assigning return costs to consumers raises the value of prominence relative to reimbursing firms by the same amount. Advertising therefore shifts the platform's preferred division of a given return bill toward consumers. We characterize the joint allocation for small positive return losses and give a cost condition under which the platform pays nothing. In markets with frequent returns, the platform can instead share the bill with consumers: a higher commission makes it pay more to encourage shopping and retained sales. Results at finite losses show that advertising can change the optimal policy from firm-paid free returns to full consumer payment, reducing both commissions and consumer surplus. This advertising-induced policy change can lower or raise total welfare, depending on whether savings from fewer trials and returns offset the loss from reduced. participation.

authors.name: Yufan Wu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Jun Yu
authors.institution: National Clinical Research Center for Digestive Diseases

papers.title: When Anchors Shift the Target: Advantage-Gated Adaptation for Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Forward-process reinforcement learning adapts diffusion and flow-matching models by re-noising rewarded generations into regression targets. Because negative advantages induce concave updates with unbounded repulsive gradients, existing methods stabilize training using cached predictions from a moving policy copy, yet these anchors also alter what positive feedback teaches the model to fit. We formalize this conflict as anchor coupling: after separating frozen-reference regularizers, affine moving-anchor rules cannot eliminate negative curvature while preserving every positive regression target. We propose Advantage-Gated Adaptation (AGA) to decouple these roles. Positive samples retain standard target fitting, whose self-limiting update vanishes at the observed target independently of the moving anchor. Negative samples instead use the first-order tangent of the concave objective at the moving-policy prediction, preserving the local repulsion direction with a prediction-independent gradient. Within the quadratic-anchor family, these requirements uniquely determine the parameter-free gate $\omega(a)=\max(-a,0)$. Because the moving copy provides local linearization rather than retention, AGA assigns long-horizon behavior preservation to a frozen pretrained reference regularized at its operating classifier-free guidance scale, interpreted through an implicit-reward lens. Across compositional generation, text rendering, and preference alignment, our experiments show that displacing positive targets degrades visual quality and heightens sensitivity to policy-copy schedules, whereas AGA consistently improves the reward--quality trade-off.

papers.title: Sample-efficient Personalization of Large Language Model Alignment with Multidimensional User Preference Data
papers.abstract: Preference alignment has become a central tool to align large language models (LLMs) with human values and desired behavior, and its online variant can further advance their capabilities beyond what static data alone offer by repeatedly generating and labeling new responses with human feedback. But costly, time-consuming annotations limit its scalability, making sample efficiency essential, and existing methods typically seek to improve it by expanding coverage of the response space or selecting pairs with the highest uncertainty for comparison. Although they are effective, these methods quantify uncertainty from the perspective of the LLM, which may differ from the uncertainty perceived by the user: a pair can appear highly uncertain to the LLM even when past comparisons from the user already imply a clear ordering. In this paper, we propose multidimensional preference-guided online direct preference optimization (MPG-DPO), which leverages low-cost multidimensional evaluations from automated verifiers on the user historical comparisons to construct a personalized preference cone guiding response selection for online preference alignment. Specifically, it first discards responses that are confidently dominated under the estimated user preference, then selects two responses that are competitive under the retained preference cone yet exhibit the strongest unresolved disagreement. Theoretical analysis shows that, with high probability, the fraction of queries spent on cone-dominated responses vanishes as learning progresses. Experiments across multiple LLM families show that MPG-DPO outperforms strong contenders under matched query budgets.

papers.title: $L^p$-norms of holomorphic cusp forms
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal orders of local and global $L^p$-norms of $L^2$-normalized holomorphic cusp forms of large weight on the modular surface, for fixed $2<p\leq\infty$. Both orders are attained by peak forms. For normalized Poincar\'e series of weight $k$ and index $m$, we obtain an asymptotic formula with an explicit constant, uniformly for $1\leq m\leq c_0k$ with any fixed $c_0<(4\pi)^{-1}$. We also give sup norm bounds in a wider range of indices.

papers.title: OfficePrism: Benchmarking Agents on Single-Domain Operations Across Enterprise Business Functions
papers.abstract: Broad workplace scores can mix competence within one business function with the extra cost of coordinating across functions and systems, making failures hard to localize. OfficePrism evaluates this prerequisite through 420 single-domain enterprise tasks spanning seven business functions under shared, benchmark-defined L1--L3 task-structure levels. Each task runs in a fresh environment combining a shared synthetic organization with one function-specific domain and yped state access. Our pipeline uses grounded records, business rules, and tool schemas to jointly construct a Chinese-language ticket, a hidden executable reference witness, and an expected response, followed by automated filtering and human curation. The same task set is evaluated through full-schema and search-and-dispatch packages. Across 124 model--harness--package configurations, the per-case joint natural-language-and-database pass rate ranges from 22.6% to 76.4%, with a median of 67.9%. L1 is highest in all 124 configurations, and L2 exceeds L3 in 122. Among 50 configurations sharing the same harness and model labels across both packages, search scores higher in 30, ties in one, and scores lower in 19.

papers.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models
papers.abstract: Physical agents must use what they previously saw or touched after visibility or contact is lost. Their actions change the implications of these remembered facts. We introduce executable perceptual memory (EPM), a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination. Its evolving read-out informs reward prediction, value estimation and policy learning. We align reward inputs with the transitions that produced them and supervise the reward head on open-loop rollouts of recorded actions. On Memory Maze $13\times13$, EPM reaches 30.37 return at 1M interactions, compared with 23.37 when the same evolving read-out informs only policy and value on a common perceptual front end: a gain of 7.00 [3.80, 10.21]. The complete method also improves control on $9\times9$ and in MiniWorld. Probes of remembered, out-of-view arrivals show stronger reward anticipation in both visual implementations. Concentration, tactile recovery and real tactile frames demonstrate complementary roles of remembered facts in imagined-policy training, motion-dependent decisions and sensory-content retention. EPM connects persistent perception to the predicted consequences and learning signals of a world model for Physical AI.

papers.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
papers.abstract: We prove the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume bound for lattice polytopes with $k\ge3$ interior lattice points: the Euclidean volume of such a lattice polytope is at most $6(k+1)$, with equality if and only if the polytope is affinely unimodularly equivalent to $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,3e_2,6(k+1)e_3)$. The inequality is strict when the minimum lattice width is at least three. Together with the known cases $k=1,2$, this completely resolves the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture.

papers.title: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Smart-Contract Fuzzing: Why Online Feedback Fails to Improve Vulnerability Triage
papers.abstract: Smart-contract fuzzing campaigns share a finite budget and vary widely in the execution cost of a first correct-class vulnerability report. Using trace replay on 143 annotated and 350 bug-injected contracts, we test whether online feedback improves triage. At a mean budget of 100 executions per contract, uniform allocation reaches 72% and 70% of the respective clairvoyant optima. All eight online policies trail uniform on aggregate triage, as do the seven repeated on the bug-injected corpus. Five online signals yield ranking AUCs of 0.32-0.51 for imminent reports. Synthetic-oracle experiments show that sufficiently accurate detection-cost estimates recover more of the gap than detectability rankings. This motivates an offline probability-curve allocator that predicts first-report probabilities across budgets and allocates by predicted gain per execution. In a frozen evaluation on four fresh seeds per corpus, detection-budget AUC improves over uniform by 5.38% and 4.81% on the two source corpora and by 1.99-6.54% on three additional public benchmark subsets.

authors.name: Yanzi Liu

papers.title: Magnetic History and Field Sweep Rate Effects on Transformation Hysteresis in $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$
papers.abstract: Hysteresis in magnetic-field-induced structural phase transformations is a major obstacle to the application of metamagnetic shape memory alloys. One promising approach to reduce hysteresis is to utilize a metastable martensitic state generated by magnetic-field cycling. However, the mechanism by which the metastable state reduces hysteresis remains unclear. Here, microsecond pulsed-field magnetization measurements are used to investigate the transformation kinetics of $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$. Magnetic-field cycling reduces the hysteresis width by approximately 50-60%, demonstrating that substantial suppression persists on a microsecond timescale. Comparison with millisecond pulsed-field measurements suggests that the reverse martensitic transformation field is more sensitive to the field sweep rate for the metastable martensite than for the initial martensite. Possible explanations include enhanced thermal activation associated with a lower effective activation barrier and differences in the athermal contribution arising from different metastable martensitic microstructures.

authors.name: X. Xu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Distilling World Action Models for Efficient Bimanual Manipulation via Anchored Path Matching
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising. Few-step distillation reduces the number of model evaluations, but its coarse updates can move the student away from the teacher's trajectory. We propose Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student. From each state, we continue the teacher to zero noise and use its endpoint and first intermediate state as targets. Modality-routed adapters learn to match both targets from the same starting state. When the two gradients conflict, anchor-priority updates preserve the endpoint gradient and remove the opposing component of the local gradient within each modality. One checkpoint supports 1-, 2-, and 4-step joint generation. The sampling budget can be chosen at deployment without retraining or teacher queries. On RoboTwin 2.0, we train only on Clean demonstrations and evaluate directly on the domain-randomized Random setting. At one step, APM improves closed-loop success over continued base distillation at matched inference budgets by 2.0 percentage points on Clean and 1.4 on Random. Video peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) rises from 30.169 to 32.317 dB, with gains in structural similarity (SSIM) and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). On two real-robot tasks, APM improves success over the one-step teacher and reduces control-cycle latency by $21.3\times$ relative to the eight-step teacher.Project page: https://jialonglong.github.io/Anchored-Path-Matching/.

authors.name: Bin Zhou
authors.institution: University of Tennessee Health Science Center

papers.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
papers.abstract: Executing an idea often changes how promising it looks, so the next step in autonomous research should rest on results, not on proposals. After each round of experiments, the system must decide whether to refine the best solution or start a new direction, which solution to build from, and what goal to set. We call this the between-round decision. Existing systems wrap it in machinery such as rules, scores, search trees, and schedules; where an LLM makes it, what the LLM needs to read is left open. We ask whether an LLM can make this decision from accumulated evidence, without a search structure around it, and how much of that evidence it needs to read. We present BRED (Between-Round Evidence-based Decision), an LLM-based controller that maintains the best verified solution so far (the Champion) and a log of past rounds, and makes one decision per round. On three widely used research-agent benchmark tasks, BRED improves on the task baselines by 4.80% in MAE on ETTh1 (to 0.4172) and by 3.44 and 3.43 points of accuracy on SST-2 (to 95.07%) and CIFAR-100 (to 84.63%), ahead of the published results. When the controller does not read the accumulated evidence, the same loop gains less: with no history it reaches 0.4299 on ETTh1 and 83.71% on CIFAR-100, whereas the full controller's MAE is 2.95% lower and its accuracy 0.92 points higher. On a new task, speech-based depression detection under a leakage-free protocol, it reaches a macro-F1 of 0.6164 on seeds held out from selection, 5.5 points above its baseline and 4.0 above the strongest published system. Code is available at https://github.com/learninginvision/BRED.

papers.title: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with general bulk viscosity
papers.abstract: The global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the two-dimensional repulsive Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum. The periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with a positive constant background are treated under a common growth condition on the viscosity primitive. The coefficient class includes every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. A density upper bound and low-order estimates, uniform in time and independent of a positive density lower bound, are obtained without an initial acceleration compatibility condition. Exponential relaxation is proved on the torus, and qualitative convergence to equilibrium is established in the whole space under a finite electric energy condition and without spatial moment assumptions. If the initial density vanishes at a point, the vacuum persists and density gradients become unbounded as time tends to infinity.

papers.title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
papers.abstract: We investigate communication-efficient federated learning over heterogeneous datasets in the presence of Byzantine adversaries capable of uploading arbitrary information. Penalty-based methods bound the influence of each worker through the bounded gradient of a penalty function; however, the bound is lost once the uploads are compressed, since a Byzantine worker can accumulate an unbounded state at the server. To retain the Byzantine resilience under compressed uploads, we propose a projected penalty-gradient tracking framework, where each honest worker uploads a compressed residual of its penalty gradient and the server projects each reconstructed state onto the known penalty-gradient ball. The framework accommodates any contractive compressor and yields two algorithms: fault-resilient proximal gradient with consistent sparsification (FRPG-CS), whose shared mask is protected by freshly drawn reserve rows, and lazily aggregated FRPG (LAG-FRPG), whose uploads are event-triggered. For smooth and strongly convex losses, we establish a finite-time bound on the expected objective gap, where the Byzantine error floor is independent of the compressor and the compression error decays faster than the optimization error. We also bound the expected number of lazy uploads and derive certificates that separate the finite-penalty model bias from the optimization error. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST show that the proposed algorithms attain the highest accuracy among twelve methods under the Min-Max attack, whereas a compressed-momentum benchmark and a local-update benchmark remain preferable in attack-free accuracy and total traffic, respectively.

papers.title: Grid-Aware Assessment of Forced Oscillations from Spatially Distributed Large Loads
papers.abstract: This paper develops a unified analytical framework for assessing forced oscillations induced by spatially distributed large-load fluctuations to determine their grid-aware fluctuation magnitudes. Emerging computational loads, such as hyperscale datacenters, present cyclic power variations with dynamic impacts depending on the waveform characteristics, forcing frequency, and source location. Our grid-aware framework represents these fluctuations using deterministic harmonic and probabilistic spectral models, and analyzes the resulting bus-wise frequency deviations based on a generic grid frequency-response model. Deterministic, risk-aware, and band-based probabilistic severity measures are further developed to obtain admissible fluctuation limits under different assumptions on frequency and phase uncertainty. We also formulate a security-constrained (SC) optimization of locational fluctuation magnitudes among existing large loads, accounting for their aggregated frequency deviation level. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus and 14-generator Australian systems validate the proposed severity measures and admissible limit analysis. The SC optimization results further show that distributing a given amount of aggregate fluctuation toward dynamically less sensitive locations can substantially reduce system-wide oscillation severity.

authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive experiments validate that our method advances both discriminative accuracy and fine-grained perceptual representation.

papers.title: GuardAgent: A Memory-Augmented Agentic Framework for Adaptive Detection of Adversarial Promotions in LLM-Based Recommendation
papers.abstract: In traditional recommender systems (RSs), textual information typically serves as auxiliary signals for representation learning. In contrast, in LLM-based RSs, textual information becomes the primary medium for recommendation generation through semantic understanding and reasoning. This shift fundamentally changes the attack surface, making promotion-driven manipulations more feasible, effective, and harder to detect. However, effectively detecting such attacks remains largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we present the first systematic study on detecting promotion-driven attacks against LLM-based RSs, aiming to safeguard next-generation recommendation platforms. Specifically, we propose GuardAgent, a novel LLM-powered agentic detection framework that operates through a loop of Perception, Action, Reflection and Memory. In contrast to conventional LLM-based detectors that function in a static, one-off, and opaque fashion, GuardAgent continually learns and self-evolves to adapt to unseen threat patterns while generating explainable reasoning traces and outcomes. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that GuardAgent achieves state-of-the-art generalization performance, laying the foundation for robust and trustworthy recommendation in practical settings.

papers.title: Uniform spatial Schauder estimates for backward stochastic partial differential equations with random coefficients
papers.abstract: We prove spatial Schauder estimates for super-parabolic backward stochastic partial differential equations. All coefficients can be random and depend on time and space, and the estimates are uniform in probability and time. The key ingredient is a weighted conditional energy norm adapted to the parabolic scale of each frequency block. Together with heat-kernel bounds and coefficient freezing, it controls the gradient-martingale coupling without assuming a bounded martingale integrand. As an application, we establish Schauder solvability for semilinear stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations.

papers.title: Synchronized Normalized Solutions for a Critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg System
papers.abstract:
We study positive synchronized normalized solutions to the critical
  Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg system:
  \begin{equation*}
  \left\{
  \begin{aligned}
  -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u)
  &=\lambda_1|x|^{-2a}u+\beta_1|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u
  &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(
  \mu_1|u|^{p-2}u
  +\nu\alpha|u|^{\alpha-2}u|v|^\gamma
  \right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,
  -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla v)
  &=\lambda_2|x|^{-2a}v+\beta_2|x|^{-bq}|v|^{q-2}v
  &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(
  \mu_2|v|^{p-2}v
  +\nu\gamma|u|^\alpha|v|^{\gamma-2}v
  \right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,
  \end{aligned}
  \right.
  \end{equation*}
  subject to the prescribed weighted masses
  \begin{equation*}
  \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx=\rho_1^2,
  \qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}v^2\,dx=\rho_2^2,
  \end{equation*}
  where $N\geq5$, $0\leq a<\frac{N-4}{2}$, $a<b<a+1$,
  $\alpha,\gamma>1$,
  $\alpha+\gamma=p=\frac{2N}{N-2(1+a-b)}$, $2<q<p$,
  $\beta_i,\mu_i,\rho_i>0$ for $i=1,2$, and $\nu>0$.
  The associated Lagrange multipliers
  $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\mathbb R$ are unknown.
  Under suitable algebraic compatibility conditions, we establish
  existence and multiplicity results for positive synchronized
  normalized solutions. The construction is based on synchronized
  reduction and critical energy estimates involving a finite-mass
  Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg extremal.
  In the mass-subcritical regime, we find two positive solutions
  with opposite energies when
  $\beta=\beta_1\rho_1^{q-2}=\beta_2\rho_2^{q-2}$
  is sufficiently small. In the mass-critical and mass-supercritical
  regimes, we obtain a synchronized Pohozaev ground state below the
  critical energy threshold for sufficiently small $\beta$ and for all
  $\beta>0$, respectively.

authors.name: Yifan Zhao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation. We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair. On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $\pi_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains baseline-comparable, with $1.52\times$--$1.93\times$ query speedup.

authors.name: Linfeng Zhong
